delivery_model: Benjamin leads; Sextant/AI builds; human architecture, review, acceptance and client accountability remain explicit.
financial_policy: No assumed contractor labor for software delivery. No invented owner rate, minimum price, revenue, profit, founder hours or five-awards-per-month forecast. Actual AI/compute, hosting, licenses, support and founder time must be qualified. Physical installation requires scoped specialist quotes, not assumed software labor.
factor_legend: 0=unsupported or structurally unfavorable; 1=weak; 2=limited; 3=plausible; 4=strong; 5=very strong. Profile factors are analyst judgments inferred from the saved scope/title and user-confirmed capabilities, not verified solicitation requirements. Higher barriers score means fewer expected entry barriers. Higher cash_structure means less inherent equipment/outside cash exposure, not a dollar estimate.

profiles.reason: AI/workflow engineering aligns directly with the founder's capabilities and AI-first production model.
checks: Confirm paid award structure, eligibility, submission deadline and required AI-use declarations.
Validate data access, evaluation measures, human oversight and acceptance criteria.

profiles.reason: Data modeling, application engineering and integration are strong AI-assisted delivery candidates.
checks: Determine whether this is an RFI, product purchase or custom implementation before calling it bid-ready.
Check incumbent/product constraints, migration, interfaces, pricing form and submission time.

profiles.reason: Platform and data-integration experience fits; sensitive operational data and integration scale may increase founder oversight.
checks: Review all security, access, reference, insurance and architecture requirements in the full package.
Confirm custom development is permitted, actual integration scope and acceptance obligations.

profiles.reason: A bounded application/usability improvement can fit founder-led, AI-built delivery without assuming outside developers.
checks: Obtain the actual solicitation and incumbent application/code access terms.
Confirm accessibility, testing, release ownership and measurable scope boundaries.

profiles.reason: Document workflows, data ingestion and AI-assisted integration create reusable delivery assets.
checks: Identify the selected ECM product, licensing and any required vendor authorization.
Bound migration volumes, permissions, integrations and support responsibilities.

profiles.reason: Workflow applications and reusable platform components fit the delivery model.
checks: Confirm whether a new custom platform or a named commercial product is required.
Review workflow complexity, sensitive data, integrations, hosting and acceptance criteria.

profiles.reason: AI-assisted software and training-content pipelines can be reused; subject-matter validation still requires accountable review.
checks: Confirm technical versus content scope, source-material rights and required subject-matter experts.
Check platform compatibility, assessment standards and validation expectations.

profiles.reason: Search and integration fit, but a licensing/reseller-only purchase would change the economics and route.
checks: Determine whether this is engineering/integration or primarily a license/reseller procurement.
Verify vendor authorization, license charges and migration/support scope.

profiles.reason: Workflow software and healthcare-related technical experience are relevant; product and compliance requirements are not yet verified.
checks: Determine whether an existing competency-management product and healthcare references are mandatory.
Review information security, AI governance, integrations, validation, licensing and ongoing support.

profiles.reason: Data, geospatial and workflow capabilities are relevant; domain-specific product requirements need investigation.
checks: Treat an RFI response as capture, not a paid award or an RFP submission.
Confirm assessment-domain expertise, existing product requirements and procurement timeline.

profiles.reason: Integration and platform leadership fit, but named ERP skills, coverage hours and support obligations may limit AI-only scaling.
checks: Identify the ERP product, required certifications and whether named full-time staff or support coverage is required.
Separate bounded enhancements from open-ended operational support.

profiles.reason: Identity and secure integration experience fit; product authorization and persistent operational coverage are unverified.
checks: Identify the PAM product, authorization requirements, licensing and operational SLAs.
Scope implementation separately from continuous monitoring or incident response.

profiles.reason: Integration skills apply, but a specialized dispatch platform may require proven product functionality and operational support.
checks: Verify whether custom software or an established dispatch product is acceptable.
Check operational availability, interfaces, references and implementation obligations.

profiles.reason: Data/software experience is adjacent, but specialized clinical functionality and validation could dominate effort.
checks: Confirm named product, clinical validation and reference requirements before proposing a build.
Identify accountable domain expertise and permitted AI usage.

profiles.reason: User-confirmed hydrogen installation leadership supports prime project delivery and systems integration; physical execution is a specialist field scope, not assumed software contractor labor.
checks: Confirm the prime/subcontracting structure, required engineering/safety credentials, commissioning and bonding/insurance.
Obtain installation/equipment quotes and payment schedules; outside field costs remain unknown until quoted.

profiles.reason: Systems integration and delivery leadership fit; on-site equipment/cabling may require a separate field scope.
checks: Separate software/integration work from site installation, equipment and licensed physical work.
Confirm site attendance, specialist quotes, acceptance and payment terms.

profiles.reason: Security experience is relevant, but continuous staffed response is not established by AI build capacity.
checks: Verify coverage, SOC, incident-response and staffing requirements rather than assume AI fulfills them.
Determine whether a qualified operating partner is necessary.

profiles.reason: The AI label does not remove screening hardware, OEM and operational validation dependencies.
checks: Verify OEM authorization, equipment scope, hardware pricing and relevant deployed references.
Only consider a bounded AI/integration role if permitted by the procurement.

profiles.reason: The named product may indicate a product-specific procurement rather than custom development.
checks: Verify product authorization, procurement type and whether alternatives are accepted.

profiles.reason: Specialized claims editing may be a product/domain procurement rather than an AI-first custom build.
checks: Verify product requirements, claims-domain evidence and permitted alternative approaches.

profiles.reason: Workflow and operational-platform experience fit if a custom/integration approach is permitted.
checks: Determine product versus custom-build scope, asset data, integrations, deployment and support requirements.

profiles.reason: The saved title describes incentive fulfillment, not demonstrated custom IT/AI/data or energy integration work.
checks: Reconsider only if the actual package establishes a substantive platform/integration role.
